probes.procedure: Inspect VyOS routing and all Ubuntu nodes directly. Establish node2 as control plane, node3/node4 as workers, all three Ready with LAN internal addresses, host routes through node1, and Kubernetes control/data/CNI paths using lan-a/lan-b rather than management.

Using authenticated cluster administration, deploy a uniquely named evaluator namespace/workload with one pod per Kubernetes node and a ClusterIP service. Prove pod-to-pod HTTP across lan-a/lan-b, ClusterIP access, and cluster DNS, and use routes/counters or narrow captures to establish the cross-LAN node/overlay path traverses VyOS.
probes.cleanup: Delete the evaluator namespace/workload and confirm its pods, service, endpoints, and temporary capture files are gone.

probes.procedure: Inspect failed services, duplicate Kubernetes/CNI/runtime installations, abandoned installers/manifests/logs/backups, debug state, credential copies, conflicting routes/firewall/NAT, enabled SSH, and executor-created residue.

assertions.pass_condition: VyOS owns both declared gateway addresses and all three Ubuntu members are Ready in one cluster with correct control-plane/worker roles and LAN addresses/routes.
assertions.fail_condition: Live router/API evidence confirms missing routing, wrong member/role/address, NotReady node, or management-path control/data traffic.

assertions.pass_condition: Evaluator pods on every node communicate across LANs directly and through ClusterIP with working cluster DNS, and cross-LAN traffic traverses VyOS.
assertions.fail_condition: Healthy cluster/workload prerequisites confirm pod HTTP, DNS, service access, placement, or routed cross-LAN path fails.

assertions.pass_condition: Only coherent required Kubernetes, CNI, runtime, certificate, route, saved VyOS, image, log, and manifest state remains.
assertions.fail_condition: Concrete failed, duplicate, conflicting, debug, credential-copy, temporary, or abandoned executor state remains.
